If the magnetizing current is neglected and \( \overline{I_s} = 100 \angle 0^\circ \, \text{A} \), then what is the value of the current \( \overline{I_p} \) in Ampere?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a three-phase AC power supply, connected to the three lines a, b, c on the left side of the transformer; the left transformer winding is the wye side. The right transformer windings are connected to each other to form the delta side, and are connected to the wye balanced load R, R, R on the right side, with terminals labeled A, B, C. The upper primary-side line in the figure is marked with a current arrow Ip, and the secondary-side A line is marked with a current arrow Is. There are black dot polarity marks beside each winding, used to determine the relationship between the primary and secondary current reference directions. Reasoning: According to the arrows in the figure, take the secondary-side line current Is = I_A = 100∠0° A. For a positive-sequence delta connection, the relationship between the A line current and the corresponding delta winding current is: I_sec,w = I_A/√3 ∠30°, therefore I_sec,w = 100/√3 ∠30° A. The voltage ratings are wye-side line voltage 230 V and delta-side line voltage 115 V; the wye-side per-phase voltage is 230/√3 V, and the delta-side winding voltage is equal to the line voltage 115 V, so the per-phase turns ratio a = Np/Ns = (230/√3)/115 = 2/√3. When the excitation current is ignored, the winding current is transformed according to the ideal transformer: I_pri,w = (1/a) I_sec,w. According to the dot markings in the figure and the chosen reference directions, the Ip corresponding to this problem does not need an additional 180° phase reversal. The primary side is a wye connection, and the line current is equal to the phase winding current, so Ip = I_pri,w = (√3/2)(100/√3)∠30° = 50∠30° A.

raw_record.question_text: A balanced (positive sequence) three-phase AC voltage source is connected to a balanced, star-connected load through a star-delta transformer as shown in the figure. The line-to-line voltage rating is 230 V on the star side, and 115 V on the delta side. If the magnetizing current is neglected and \( \overline{I_s} = 100 \angle 0^\circ \, \text{A} \), then what is the value of the current \( \overline{I_p} \) in ampere?

method.method_draft: First describe the image connections: identify the star primary, delta secondary, dots, and the line-current arrows. Take \(\overline I_s=I_A=100\angle0^\circ\) as the secondary line current. Convert it to the current in the relevant delta secondary winding using the positive-sequence delta relation and the shown A-B-C wiring: \(I_{sec,w}=100/\sqrt3\angle30^\circ\) A. From the voltage ratings, compute the per-phase turns ratio \(a=N_p/N_s=(230/\sqrt3)/115=2/\sqrt3\). With magnetizing current neglected, transform winding current to the primary: \(I_{pri,w}=(1/a)I_{sec,w}\), with the dot convention in the figure giving no extra 180-degree reversal for the referenced line current. Since the primary is star-connected, \(I_p=I_{pri,w}\). This gives magnitude \((\sqrt3/2)(100/\sqrt3)=50\) and angle \(+30^\circ\), so \(\overline I_p=50\angle30^\circ\) A.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中左侧是三相交流电源，接到变压器左侧的 a、b、c 三条线；左侧变压器绕组为星形侧。右侧变压器绕组相互连接成三角形侧，并接到右侧的星形平衡负载 R、R、R，端子标为 A、B、C。图中上方一次侧线路标有电流箭头 Ip，二次侧 A 线标有电流箭头 Is。各绕组旁有黑点极性标记，用于确定一次、二次电流参考方向关系。
推理：按图中箭头，取二次侧线电流 Is = I_A = 100∠0° A。对于正序三角形连接，A 线电流与相应三角形绕组电流的关系为：I_sec,w = I_A/√3 ∠30°，因此 I_sec,w = 100/√3 ∠30° A。电压额定值为星形侧线电压 230 V、三角形侧线电压 115 V；星形侧每相电压为 230/√3 V，三角形侧绕组电压等于线电压 115 V，所以每相匝比 a = Np/Ns = (230/√3)/115 = 2/√3。忽略励磁电流时，绕组电流按理想变压器变换：I_pri,w = (1/a) I_sec,w。根据图中点号及所取参考方向，本题对应的 Ip 不需再加 180° 相位反转。一次侧为星形连接，线电流等于相绕组电流，所以 Ip = I_pri,w = (√3/2)(100/√3)∠30° = 50∠30° A。

If the magnetizing current is neglected and \( \overline{I_s} = 100 \angle 0^\circ \, \text{A} \), then what is the value of the current \( \overline{I_p} \) in ampere?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A balanced (positive sequence) three-phase AC voltage source is connected to a balanced, star-connected load through a star-delta transformer as shown in the figure. The line-to-line voltage rating is 230 V on the star side, and 115 V on the delta side. If the magnetizing current is neglected and \( \overline{I_s} = 100 \angle 0^\circ \, \text{A} \), then what is the value of the current \( \overline{I_p} \) in ampere?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: On the left side of the figure is a three-phase AC power supply, connected to the three lines a, b, c on the left side of the transformer; the left transformer winding is the wye side. The right transformer windings are connected to each other to form the delta side, and are connected to the wye balanced load R, R, R on the right side, with terminals labeled A, B, C. The upper primary-side line in the figure is marked with a current arrow Ip, and the secondary-side A line is marked with a current arrow Is. There are black dot polarity marks beside each winding, used to determine the relationship between the primary and secondary current reference directions.
Reasoning: According to the arrows in the figure, take the secondary-side line current Is = I_A = 100∠0° A. For a positive-sequence delta connection, the relationship between the A line current and the corresponding delta winding current is: I_sec,w = I_A/√3 ∠30°, therefore I_sec,w = 100/√3 ∠30° A. The voltage ratings are wye-side line voltage 230 V and delta-side line voltage 115 V; the wye-side per-phase voltage is 230/√3 V, and the delta-side winding voltage is equal to the line voltage 115 V, so the per-phase turns ratio a = Np/Ns = (230/√3)/115 = 2/√3. When the excitation current is ignored, the winding current is transformed according to the ideal transformer: I_pri,w = (1/a) I_sec,w. According to the dot markings in the figure and the chosen reference directions, the Ip corresponding to this problem does not need an additional 180° phase reversal. The primary side is a wye connection, and the line current is equal to the phase winding current, so Ip = I_pri,w = (√3/2)(100/√3)∠30° = 50∠30° A.
